newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Fischer says held BHP when fuel rebate decided.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Fischer says held BHP when fuel rebate decided.

text.p: Australian Trade Minister and Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer said on Wednesday he had owned shares in The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) when he announced the government's decision to retain the diesel tax rebate.
Opposition trade spokesman Stephen Smith asked Fischer in parliament if he had owned BHP shares on August 13 when he announced the decision, which he said boosted BHP shares by A$0.20 to A$17.25.
The rebate is available to mining companies, such as BHP.
Fischer told parliament earlier he had sold his BHP shares in the last few days.

Smith also asked Fischer if he had owned BHP shares on June 14 and 15 when he visited Venezuela to raise BHP's proposed partnership with a Venezualan steel company which could lead to a US$680 million project.
Fischer did not directly respond to that question.

Earlier on Wednesday Fischer denied in a radio interview that he had breached Prime Minister John Howard's ministerial guidelines, under which government members are required to dispose of investments which might conflict with their portfolio area.
Fischer's ministerial responsibility includes promoting Australian trade.
Howard had said earlier Fischer had not breached ministerial guidelines, admitting that the guidelines might be too strict and should be reviewed.
The share row over conflict of interests has claimed two government members.
Jim Short quit as assistant treasurer on Sunday and Brian Gibson resigned from his position as parliamentary secretary to the treasurer on Tuesday.
Both resigned after their staff found evidence of interest in particular ministerial decisions.
